finding: Surviving mutant: counting every lock refusal (FileExistsError too) passes all 111 tests, yet a writer behind a live lock then gives up after ~2s instead of waiting
why: No test holds a live lock longer than the 100-refusal budget (~2s), so the reset-to-0 branch that keeps a losing writer waiting up to LOCK_WAIT is unproven, and Acceptance 'while the mutex is held the losing writer waits' rests on it.
fix: Add a test that holds a live lock past 100 polls (e.g. release_later(lock, 2.5) with default LOCK_WAIT) and asserts the write lands, not ManifestError.
evidence: Scratch-copy probe: `refusals = refusals + 1 if isinstance(exc, PermissionError) and not lock.exists() else 0` -> `refusals = refusals + 1` -> 111 passed; direct check with a lock released after 3s: original 'waited and wrote 3.0', mutant 'ManifestError cannot write the manifest of f: [WinError 183] ... 2.0'

finding: The one IOU line that D-50 relies on for adopt_manifest, remove_process and checkpoint_path is closed by the wiring gate on its next run, before any of those functions has a caller
why: The gate takes the token from the file name ('manifest' from scripts/team/manifest.py, hooks/wiring-gate.sh:174) and counts the file as wired when any other file holds that substring (hooks/lib/bounded_scan.py:89,101). scripts/tests/test_team_manifest.py and many other files already hold it, so wiring-gate.sh:235 ticks the line [x] and nothing then tracks a caller for each function.
fix: Track each function where the gate can see it, for example as Consumes lines in the 0010, 0012 and 0015 contracts (D-50 option A), or record in D-50 that the IOU is advisory only and closes as soon as the gate first runs.
evidence: wiring-gate.sh:174 'tok=${f##*/}; tok=${tok%.*}'; wiring-gate.sh:235 '_wiring_ledger_open "$f" && _wiring_ledger_close "$f"   # consumer arrived -> auto-close IOU'; bounded_scan.py:89 'if self.bytes_of[token] in data:'; diff +23 '- [ ] `scripts/team/manifest.py` -> anchor: ... calls `adopt_manifest(` ... calls `remove_process(` ... comes from `checkpoint_path(`' (also reported by scope-and-impact: The D-50 IOU will auto-close before adopt_manifest, remove_process or checkpoint_path gain a caller)

finding: The transient case (PermissionError while the lock folder still exists, i.e. being deleted) and the 100-refusal threshold have no test; both mutants survive
why: Only the always-refused case is tested, so a threshold of 1 or dropping `not lock.exists()` would fail writes during an ordinary Windows lock-folder deletion with no test noticing.
fix: Add a case where os.mkdir raises PermissionError a bounded number of times (some while the lock path exists, then succeeds) and assert the write lands; add an off-boundary case at 100 vs 101 refusals.
evidence: Scratch probe: `if refusals > 100:` -> `if refusals > 1:` -> 111 passed; `isinstance(exc, PermissionError) and not lock.exists()` -> `isinstance(exc, PermissionError)` -> 111 passed

finding: The unreadable-owner branch (`None` in `(token, None)`) is untested; replacing the check with `!= token` survives
why: Whether a writer whose lock owner file stays unreadable publishes or redoes is a deliberate choice in the new line, but no test pins it.
fix: Add a test that makes `_owner` return None during the publish (e.g. owner read raising a non-NotFound OSError) and assert the intended outcome.
evidence: Scratch probe: `if _owner(lock) not in (token, None):` -> `if _owner(lock) != token:` -> 111 passed (also reported by logic-correctness: Possible residual check-then-act window: the lock can still be stolen between the owner check and the os.replace that follows)

finding: Temp-file cleanup in finally can raise a raw PermissionError that replaces the module's ManifestError or aborts the lost-lock retry
why: Path.unlink(missing_ok=True) suppresses only FileNotFoundError, so on Windows a temp file still held open (the file-in-use case every other call here wraps in _patient) raises PermissionError from the finally block: on the except path it replaces the ManifestError, and on the `return False` path it escapes _write instead of the redo, so callers that catch ManifestError get an unexpected exception type.
fix: Route the cleanup through _patient and swallow a remaining OSError, e.g. `try: _patient(temp.unlink, True) except OSError: pass`.
evidence:
manifest.py:275-276 `finally:
        temp.unlink(missing_ok=True)`; compare :271 `_patient(os.replace, temp, path)` and :174-181 `_patient` (retries PermissionError) added for Windows file-in-use errors

finding: The mid-write steal test catches the check-before-write regression only through a 0.3s race on a leftover lock folder, not by asserting the stolen write was withheld
why: Moving the owner check back before the temp write (the bug this round fixed) fails only because release_later has not yet removed manifest.lock; on a slow runner pausing >0.3s the mutant passes, and the thief's own data is never modelled so a redo that overwrote it would go unseen.
fix: Have the thief also write a manifest change (e.g. a process entry) at steal time and assert both it and a1 survive; join the release thread; or count fsync calls == 2 to prove the redo.
evidence: Scratch probe (check moved before `with open(temp`) killed only at line 311: `AssertionError: assert ['manifest.js...anifest.lock'] == ['manifest.json']`; line 306 `release_later(lock)` thread is never joined

finding: The same 'cannot write the manifest' error is built twice in _acquire
why: Two copies of one message that callers may match on can drift apart in wording.
fix: Build the message in one place so both failures share it, for example in a small helper.
evidence: manifest.py:230 'raise ManifestError(f"cannot write the manifest of {lock.parent.name}: {exc}") from None' and manifest.py:240 'raise ManifestError(f"cannot write the manifest of {lock.parent.name}: {exc}") from None'

finding: The 'and kept' half of the non-UTF-8 test is vacuous: only read_manifest runs, which never writes
why: The bytes-unchanged assert cannot fail for a read-only call, so 'kept' is unproven for the write paths that also load the file.
fix: Also call record_entry/adopt_manifest on the non-UTF-8 file, assert ManifestError, then assert the bytes are unchanged.
evidence: `with pytest.raises(manifest.ManifestError, match="UTF-8"): manifest.read_manifest(tmp_path, FEATURE)` then `assert path.read_bytes() == b" ff fe {"`

finding: A for-loop over ("replace", "fsync") with monkeypatch.undo() mid-body drives the asserts of two cases in one test
why: A failure does not say which publish step broke, and the mid-test undo couples the cases.
fix: Parametrize on the failing os function name.
